why: The indexable layer shipped beside a /qpact report. The report itself is opaque markup the
console cannot query; this is the structure that makes a merged view across a team possible
at all — and it is therefore a second payload, with its own exposure, which is why every
field is written down here rather than inferred from whatever the spine happens to carry.
Two tiers, because they expose differently and must not default the same way.
index   bounded values and derived prose. Workspace-visible by default, so every roll-up
is complete. Nothing in it can quote a prompt.
trace   tool inputs and results in full. Author-plus-admins by default, the same rung as
the verbatim document, because a trace carries bash command lines and file
contents and exposes at least as much as the prompts above it.
WHAT THE SPINE HOLDS AND THIS REFUSES. The spine carries `file` (the absolute transcript
path, which contains the home directory and the username), `project` (the dash-encoded
project key, which contains it again), `cwd`, and `turns[].text`, which is the verbatim
prompt. None of them has a field here. The projection is written out key by key rather than
spread, so adding one is a visible edit and not an accident — the rule finding.mts states
for the nine person-blind columns, applied to a payload fifty times larger.
`repo` is the LAST SEGMENT of the working directory and never the path. `files_touched` is
repo-relative and a path that will not relativise is dropped and counted, because an
absolute path outside the repository is somebody's machine layout and not their work.

schema_version.note: This file's schema_version. A reader that does not know it refuses rather than guessing which fields mean what.

session_id.note: The harness's id. The key the console merges on, same as the report row.

repo.note: From repo.mts's repoName, which folds a worktree onto the repository it belongs to. NOT the last segment of cwd: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor each lay worktrees out differently and two of the three would yield the worktree, fragmenting a team roll-up into one repository per checkout.

branch.note: Carries whatever a person put in a branch name, which is sometimes their own.

title.note: The harness's own session title. Model-written, and it can paraphrase a prompt.

score.value.note: null for a session with no scored turns. SessionScore says so; a reader that coerces null to 0 reports a perfect-worst session that was never measured.

score.band.note: Five bands, not three. Taken from ScoreBand in extract.mts rather than from memory.

score.friction_rate.note: Optional on SessionScore — absent for a session with no turns, so it is emitted as null rather than 0.

score.craft_rate.note: Optional on SessionScore — absent for a session with no turns, so it is emitted as null rather than 0.

score.wasted_tokens.note: Optional on SessionScore — absent for a session with no turns, so it is emitted as null rather than 0.

score.costliest_turn.note: Optional on SessionScore — absent for a session with no turns, so it is emitted as null rather than 0.

tools.note: tool NAME -> calls. Never an input.

files_touched.note: TurnFileTouch.path is ALREADY relative to the session's working directory, with '../' when the file sits outside it. So the rule here is not relativisation, it is escape: a path beginning '../' names something outside the repository — machine layout, not work — and is dropped and counted in files_dropped.

turns.note: Per turn: index, duration_ms, tool_calls, tokens_output, friction, score. Shape only — no text, no files, no tool inputs. turns[].files is refused here even though it is relative, because per-turn paths reconstruct a working session in a way the aggregate list does not.

trace_shape.note: tool name -> calls in the trace tier, so a roll-up can describe a trace nobody reading it is allowed to open.

intents.note: Model-written. Title, status and cited turns — no summary body, because a summary paraphrases prompts and this tier is workspace-visible.

graph.note: Model-written concepts and relations. Concept and relation labels are prose and can paraphrase a prompt — the one index field where that is true, and why intents drop their summaries; a label that quotes a prompt is withheld before it leaves. Notes, anchors and provenance never cross. Ids must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ or the concept is dropped with its relations.

trace.note: Per call: turn, seq, tool, mcp_server, started_at, duration_ms, ok, error_kind, input, result, input_bytes, result_bytes, truncated. Inputs and results in full — bash command lines, file contents, MCP arguments. Sourced from extract's --with-trace, which is off by default and records in the spine which happened; a result is cut at the extractor's ceiling with its original length carried in result_bytes, so a truncation is never reported as the whole answer.

paths_recorded.note: Extract's recordedPaths is TRI-STATE and its header is explicit that absence must never be read as false. Without this field an empty files_touched is indistinguishable from a session that touched nothing, and the comfortable reading is the wrong one. A merged view that counted 'files touched' across a team would silently under-report every machine that ran with --no-paths.

secrets_redacted.note: Whether the spine went through the secret patterns. Recorded because --no-redact exists and nothing downstream can observe it by looking — the evidence package once asserted a redaction that had not happened, over the top of the unredacted key. It sits in the INDEX tier deliberately, even though it describes the trace: a reader deciding whether to open a trace needs it before they open it.

worktree.note: The second axis. Kept rather than folded away, because two checkouts of one repository are otherwise indistinguishable.

input.note: Secret-redacted by extract, which is pattern matching and not the same as safe.

result.note: Truncated per call; the original length is kept in result_bytes so a reader can see what was cut.

refuses.file: the absolute transcript path — contains the home directory and the username
refuses.project: the dash-encoded project key — contains the home directory and the username again
refuses.turns[].toolCalls: raw tool calls; the trace tier carries these deliberately and separately
refuses.turns[].signals: prompt shape — chars, words, isQuestion, isCorrection. Derived from the prompt text, and a fingerprint of it
